content.text:
The bug is fixed! The issue was floating-point precision errors in three price-parsing functions: `parseEuros`, `cellCents`, and `decimalCommaToCents`. When multiplying decimal values by 100 to convert to cents, JavaScript produces imprecise results (39.95 × 100 = 3995.0000000000005). Adding `Math.round()` after the multiplication ensures whole cent values that pass validation.

All tests pass and your subscriptions now work:
- ✅ Gym: €39.95/month
- ✅ Netflix: €12.99/month  
- ✅ Spotify: €10.99/month

Ready to commit these changes when you approve.
